tasks.title: 프로젝트 초기 설정 및 기본 구조 구축
tasks.description: Node.js, TypeScript, Express를 사용하여 Idle RPG 서버의 기본 프로젝트 구조를 설정하고, 상태 확인을 위한 기본 엔드포인트를 구현합니다.
tasks.details:
이 작업은 프로젝트의 기반을 마련합니다. `package.json` 분석 결과, Express와 TypeScript가 이미 설정되어 있습니다. 이 구조를 바탕으로 초기 설정을 완료합니다.
1. `npm install`을 실행하여 `package.json`에 명시된 의존성(express, typescript 등)을 모두 설치합니다.
2. `src/` 디렉토리 내에 서버의 메인 로직을 담을 `server.ts`와 서버를 실행시킬 `index.ts` 파일을 생성합니다. (`E:\StudyGameProj\IdleRPGServer\src\` 경로 확인)
3. `server.ts` 파일에서 Express 애플리케이션 인스턴스를 생성하고 export하는 함수 `createServer()`를 구현합니다. 이 함수는 기본적인 미들웨어(예: `express.json()`)를 포함해야 합니다.
4. 서버의 상태를 확인할 수 있도록 `/health` GET 엔드포인트를 추가합니다. 이 엔드포인트는 `200 OK` 상태 코드와 `{ status: 'ok' }` JSON 응답을 반환해야 합니다.
5. `index.ts` 파일에서 `server.ts`의 `createServer()` 함수를 import하고, 환경 변수 또는 기본값으로 포트를 설정하여 서버를 시작하는 로직을 구현합니다.
6. `tsconfig.json` 파일에서 컴파일 옵션(예: `"outDir": "./dist"`, `"rootDir": "./src"`)이 올바르게 설정되었는지 확인합니다.
7. `package.json`의 `scripts`에 `"start": "node dist/index.js"`, `"build": "tsc"`, `"dev": "ts-node-dev --respawn src/index.ts"` 와 같은 실행 스크립트를 정의하여 개발 및 배포 편의성을 확보합니다.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. 터미널에서 `npm run dev` 명령어를 실행하여 개발 서버가 오류 없이 시작되는지 확인합니다.
2. 웹 브라우저나 Postman과 같은 API 테스트 도구를 사용하여 `http://localhost:3000/health` (포트는 설정에 따라 다를 수 있음)로 GET 요청을 보냅니다.
3. 응답 상태 코드가 `200`이고, 응답 본문이 `{"status":"ok"}` JSON 객체와 일치하는지 확인합니다.
4. `npm run build` 명령어를 실행하여 `src` 디렉토리의 TypeScript 파일들이 `dist` 디렉토리에 JavaScript 파일로 성공적으로 컴파일되는지 확인합니다.
5. `npm start` 명령어를 실행하여 컴파일된 파일로 서버가 정상적으로 구동되는지 확인하고, 다시 한번 `/health` 엔드포인트를 테스트합니다.

tasks.title: Define SkillRarity and SkillType Enums
tasks.description: Create the enumerations for skill rarity (Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary) and skill type (e.g., Active, Passive) in the Domain layer.
tasks.details: In the `IdleGameServer.Domain` project, create a new folder `Enums`. Inside, create `SkillRarity.cs` and `SkillType.cs`. These enums will be used throughout the gacha system, especially in the Skill entity.
tasks.testStrategy: No specific tests required for enums, but they will be validated by their usage in other components' tests.

tasks.title: Define Skill Entity
tasks.description: Create the `Skill` entity in the Domain layer to store skill properties.
tasks.details: In the `IdleGameServer.Domain/Entities` folder, create `Skill.cs`. The entity should include properties like `Id` (int), `Name` (string), `Description` (string), `Rarity` (SkillRarity), and `Type` (SkillType). It should inherit from a base entity if one exists.
tasks.testStrategy: Entity property validation will be covered by EF Core model configuration tests and integration tests.

tasks.title: Define PlayerSkill Entity
tasks.description: Create the `PlayerSkill` entity to represent the link between a player and a skill they own.
tasks.details: In `IdleGameServer.Domain/Entities`, create `PlayerSkill.cs`. This will be a join table entity. It should contain `PlayerId`, `SkillId`, and `Level` (int). Define navigation properties back to `Player` and `Skill`.
tasks.testStrategy: Database relationship integrity will be tested via integration tests that add skills to a player.

tasks.title: Define GachaPool Entity
tasks.description: Create the `GachaPool` entity to define the items available in a specific gacha banner.
tasks.details: In `IdleGameServer.Domain/Entities`, create `GachaPool.cs`. This entity will link a gacha banner/pool (e.g., 'StandardSkillGacha') to a specific skill and its draw weight/probability. Properties should include `Id`, `PoolName` (string), `SkillId` (int), and `Weight` (int or double).
tasks.testStrategy: Correct loading and interpretation of this data will be tested in the `GachaService` unit tests.

tasks.title: Define Gacha-related Repository Interfaces
tasks.description: Define the contracts for data access in the Domain layer for all new entities.
tasks.details: In the `IdleGameServer.Domain/Interfaces` (or equivalent) folder, create `ISkillRepository.cs`, `IPlayerSkillRepository.cs`, and `IGachaRepository.cs`. These interfaces should define methods for CRUD operations, such as `GetByIdAsync`, `AddAsync`, and any specific query methods needed (e.g., `GetPoolByNameAsync` for `IGachaRepository`).
tasks.testStrategy: Interfaces themselves are not tested, but their implementations will be.

tasks.title: Add New DbSets to AppDbContext
tasks.description: Update the application's DbContext to include the new entities.
tasks.details: In the `IdleGameServer.Infrastructure/Data/AppDbContext.cs` file, add `DbSet<Skill> Skills { get; set; }`, `DbSet<PlayerSkill> PlayerSkills { get; set; }`, and `DbSet<GachaPool> GachaPools { get; set; }`.
tasks.testStrategy: Successful migration creation will serve as an initial validation. Further validation in integration tests.

tasks.title: Configure New Entities in AppDbContext
tasks.description: Use the Fluent API to configure relationships, keys, and constraints for the new entities.
tasks.details: In `AppDbContext.cs`, override the `OnModelCreating` method. Add configurations for `Skill`, `PlayerSkill`, and `GachaPool`. Define primary keys, foreign keys (e.g., `PlayerSkill` to `Player` and `Skill`), and any indexes or constraints needed (e.g., a unique constraint on `PlayerSkill` for `PlayerId` and `SkillId`).
tasks.testStrategy: A successful database migration is the primary test. Integration tests will confirm relationship behavior.

tasks.title: Create EF Core Migration for Gacha Schema
tasks.description: Generate a new database migration script based on the DbContext changes.
tasks.details: Using the .NET CLI or Package Manager Console, run the `dotnet ef migrations add AddGachaSystem` command. Verify that the generated migration script correctly creates the `Skills`, `PlayerSkills`, and `GachaPools` tables with the right columns and constraints.
tasks.testStrategy: Review the generated migration file for correctness. Apply the migration to a local development database to ensure it runs without errors.

tasks.title: Add Currency Property to Player Entity
tasks.description: Add a 'Crystals' property to the existing Player entity to be used as currency for gacha.
tasks.details: Locate the `Player.cs` entity in the `IdleGameServer.Domain` project. Add a new property: `public long Crystals { get; set; }`. After adding the property, generate a new EF Core migration (`AddCrystalsToPlayer`) and apply it to the database.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the new column is added to the `Players` table after applying the migration. Integration tests for gacha will confirm it can be read and updated.

tasks.title: Implement SkillRepository
tasks.description: Create the concrete implementation of the ISkillRepository interface.
tasks.details: In the `IdleGameServer.Infrastructure/Repositories` folder, create `SkillRepository.cs`. Implement the methods defined in `ISkillRepository` using the `AppDbContext` to query the `Skills` table.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test repository methods with an in-memory database or mock DbContext. Integration tests will cover real database interaction.

tasks.title: Implement PlayerSkillRepository
tasks.description: Create the concrete implementation of the IPlayerSkillRepository interface.
tasks.details: In `IdleGameServer.Infrastructure/Repositories`, create `PlayerSkillRepository.cs`. Implement methods for adding new skills to a player's inventory and querying their existing skills.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test repository methods with an in-memory database or mock DbContext. Integration tests will cover real database interaction.

tasks.title: Implement GachaRepository
tasks.description: Create the implementation for IGachaRepository to load gacha pool data.
tasks.details: In `IdleGameServer.Infrastructure/Repositories`, create `GachaRepository.cs`. Implement the `GetPoolByNameAsync` method. The data can be loaded from a dedicated `gacha-pools.json` file in the project (read on startup and cached) or from the `GachaPools` table in the database.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test the repository to ensure it correctly parses the JSON file or queries the database and constructs the `GachaPool` objects.

tasks.title: Create Data Seeding Logic for Skills and Gacha Pools
tasks.description: Populate the database with initial skill and gacha probability data.
tasks.details: Create a seeder class or use EF Core's `HasData` method in `OnModelCreating`. Define a set of initial skills (e.g., 10-20 skills across different rarities) and configure the 'StandardSkillGacha' pool in the `GachaPools` table, assigning weights to each skill.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the application and verify that the `Skills` and `GachaPools` tables are populated with the correct initial data.

tasks.title: Implement GachaService Domain Service
tasks.description: Create the core domain service responsible for performing the weighted random draw.
tasks.details: In `IdleGameServer.Domain/Services`, create `GachaService.cs`. This service will have a method like `DrawSkills(IEnumerable<GachaPoolItem> pool, int count)`. The method will take a gacha pool and the number of items to draw, and return a list of selected `Skill` entities based on their weights.
tasks.testStrategy: This service is critical and must be unit tested thoroughly. See Task 16.

tasks.title: Unit Test GachaService Probability Logic
tasks.description: Write comprehensive unit tests for the GachaService to ensure its correctness.
tasks.details: Create a test project for the Domain layer if one doesn't exist. Write tests for `GachaService`. Mock the gacha pool data. Run a large number of draws (e.g., 1,000,000) and assert that the distribution of results is within an acceptable tolerance of the defined weights/probabilities. Test edge cases like an empty pool or drawing zero items.
tasks.testStrategy: Use a statistical approach to verify probability distribution. For a skill with 10% probability, after 1M draws, the result count should be close to 100,000.

tasks.title: Define Application Layer DTOs and Commands
tasks.description: Create the Command and DTO objects for the gacha feature in the Application layer.
tasks.details: In the `IdleGameServer.Application` project, create `PerformGachaCommand.cs` which will contain `PlayerId` and `DrawCount`. Also create `GachaResultDto.cs` which will contain a list of the acquired skills (e.g., `List<SkillDto>`). Create a `SkillDto` to represent a simplified view of a skill for the client.
tasks.testStrategy: These are data structures; their validation is implicit in the integration tests of the application service.

tasks.title: Define IPlayerCurrencyService Interface
tasks.description: Define an interface to abstract currency operations, promoting loose coupling.
tasks.details: In the `IdleGameServer.Application/Common/Interfaces` folder, create `IPlayerCurrencyService.cs`. It should define methods like `Task<bool> HasSufficientCurrencyAsync(string playerId, long amount)` and `Task DeductCurrencyAsync(string playerId, long amount)`.
tasks.testStrategy: Interface is not tested directly. Its implementation will be tested.

tasks.title: Implement PlayerCurrencyService
tasks.description: Create a concrete implementation of the IPlayerCurrencyService.
tasks.details: In a suitable folder within the `IdleGameServer.Application` project, create `PlayerCurrencyService.cs`. This service will use the `IPlayerRepository` (via `IUnitOfWork`) to fetch player data, check their crystal balance, and update it.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test the service logic with a mocked `IUnitOfWork` and `IPlayerRepository` to verify correct balance checking and deduction logic.

tasks.title: Update IUnitOfWork Interface
tasks.description: Extend the existing IUnitOfWork interface to include the new repositories.
tasks.details: In `IdleGameServer.Application/Common/Interfaces/IUnitOfWork.cs`, add properties for the new repository interfaces: `ISkillRepository Skills { get; }`, `IPlayerSkillRepository PlayerSkills { get; }`, `IGachaRepository GachaPools { get; }`. Update the concrete `UnitOfWork` implementation in Infrastructure as well.
tasks.testStrategy: Compilation success and proper function in integration tests will validate this change.

tasks.title: Implement GachaApplicationService
tasks.description: Create the application service to orchestrate the entire gacha workflow.
tasks.details: In `IdleGameServer.Application/Services`, create `GachaApplicationService.cs`. This service will handle the `PerformGachaCommand`. Its logic will be: 1. Calculate total cost. 2. Use `IPlayerCurrencyService` to check and deduct crystals. 3. Use `IGachaRepository` to get the pool. 4. Use `GachaService` to draw skills. 5. Use `IPlayerSkillRepository` to save the results. 6. Commit transaction with `IUnitOfWork`. 7. Return `GachaResultDto`.
tasks.testStrategy: The full workflow will be tested via integration tests. Unit tests can be written by mocking all dependencies (`IUnitOfWork`, services, etc.) to test the orchestration logic in isolation.

tasks.title: Create GachaController API Endpoint
tasks.description: Expose the gacha functionality through a new API endpoint.
tasks.details: In the `IdleGameServer.Api/Controllers` folder, create `GachaController.cs`. Create a `POST` endpoint at `/api/gacha/draw`. This endpoint will accept the `PerformGachaCommand` in its body, pass it to the `GachaApplicationService`, and return the `GachaResultDto` with a 200 OK status or an appropriate error response (e.g., 400 Bad Request for insufficient funds).
tasks.testStrategy: Endpoint behavior will be fully tested via integration tests (Task 24).

tasks.title: Register New Services for Dependency Injection
tasks.description: Wire up all the new interfaces and implementations in the DI container.
tasks.details: In `IdleGameServer.Api/Program.cs` (or a service registration extension method), add scoped registrations for all new services and repositories. For example: `services.AddScoped<ISkillRepository, SkillRepository>();`, `services.AddScoped<IGachaApplicationService, GachaApplicationService>();`, etc.
tasks.testStrategy: The application successfully starting and the API endpoint working correctly in integration tests will confirm proper DI configuration.

tasks.title: Create Integration Tests for Gacha Endpoint
tasks.description: Write end-to-end tests for the gacha API endpoint.
tasks.details: In the integration test project, create `GachaControllerTests.cs`. Use `WebApplicationFactory` to set up an in-memory test server. Write tests that: 1. Create a test player with sufficient crystals. 2. Send a POST request to `/api/gacha/draw` for 1x and 10x draws. 3. Assert a 200 OK response and a valid `GachaResultDto`. 4. Verify in the test database that crystals were deducted and skills were added. 5. Test the failure case where a player has insufficient crystals and assert a 400 Bad Request response.
tasks.testStrategy: This is a full end-to-end test using a real (in-memory or test container) database to validate the entire feature from API request to database state change.

tasks.title: Document Gacha API and Configuration
tasks.description: Document the new API endpoint and the format for gacha configuration.
tasks.details: Update the project's API documentation (e.g., Swagger/OpenAPI annotations on the controller action) to describe the `/api/gacha/draw` endpoint, its request body, and possible responses. Create or update a `README.md` or wiki page explaining how to configure the gacha pools, especially if using a JSON file (`gacha-pools.json`), detailing its structure and how weights are interpreted.
tasks.testStrategy: Peer review of the documentation for clarity and accuracy. Manually check that Swagger UI displays the information correctly.
